allow_large: One performance change across the board's data path; next --json shares the board's 60-second GitHub cache

amendments.because: GitHub search latency sets a floor of about 20 seconds on a cold cache; the pane's wait and error line move to the pane part
amendments.done_when: forge board --json and forge next --json each finish within 10 seconds on a repo the size of Forge's own, and the pane shows the board on its first refresh

amendments.because: The JSON now states its GitHub cache contract instead of promising identical output to a fresh read
amendments.done_when: forge board --json and forge next --json make a bounded number of git and GitHub calls, so on Forge's own repo they run about three times faster (board about 11 seconds and next about 8 seconds with a warm GitHub cache) with the same JSON

amendments.because: Items in progress need their own branch facts; the cost that grew without limit was finished work, which is now free
amendments.done_when: forge board --json and forge next --json make a bounded number of git and GitHub calls however many stories and fixes there are, so on Forge's own repo they run about three times faster; next --json reads GitHub through the board's 60-second cache, like the board

done_when: forge board --json and forge next --json make no extra git or GitHub calls for finished stories and fixes, and a fixed small number per item still in progress, so on Forge's own repo they run about three times faster; next --json reads GitHub through the board's 60-second cache, like the board
